recreation_brief: 1. Set the slide background to light gray (#F0F0F0).
2. Draw a thin red (#FF0000) rectangle border framing the full slide perimeter; it must enclose every other element on the slide.
3. Place a yellow (#FFFF00) filled circle with a black (#000000) outline in the top-right corner (center at approx 95% x, 5% y) and center the bold black numeral '9' inside it.
4. Build the left chart panel as a rectangular area spanning approx 5%–48% x and 15%–80% y: fill it #F5F5F5 and overlay #CCCCCC grid lines (the source documents no panel border).
5. Inside the left panel, draw red (#FF0000) arrow shapes for the x-axis and the y-axis.

6. Scatter approximately 10–12 orange (#FFA500) filled circular data points across the left panel in a loose linear trend from lower-left to upper-right (exact count not specified in the source; see uncertain_items).

7. Draw a straight blue (#0000FF) fitted line through the left panel from lower-left to upper-right, angled to pass close to the orange points while leaving clear space above it for the outlier placed in the next step.
8. Add exactly one solid red (#FF0000) filled circular outlier point above the fitted line, clearly separated from the orange points.
9. Draw thin red (#FF0000) residual arrows from the fitted line to the nearby orange points, one arrow per nearby point (exact count not specified in the source; see uncertain_items).
10. Place a light-blue (#E0F0FF) rectangular text box near the top of the left panel containing the black (#000000) text '50.85² = 2585'.
11. Place a vertical double-headed red (#FF0000) arrow to the left of the red outlier point and write the black (#000000) label '50.85 mm' beside it.
12. Build the right chart panel as a rectangular area spanning approx 52%–95% x and 15%–80% y, matching the left panel: #F5F5F5 fill, #CCCCCC grid lines, and red (#FF0000) x- and y-axis arrows.

13. Scatter approximately 10–12 orange (#FFA500) filled circular data points in the right panel in a clear linear trend from lower-left to upper-right, clustered tightly along that trend; this panel contains no red outlier point (exact count not specified in the source; see uncertain_items).
14. Draw a straight blue (#0000FF) fitted line from lower-left to upper-right that follows the general trend of the orange points without bending toward any single point.
15. Draw thin red (#FF0000) residual arrows from the fitted line to the orange points, one arrow per nearby point (exact count not specified in the source; see uncertain_items).
16. Place a light-blue (#E0F0FF) rectangular text box near the top of the right panel containing the black (#000000) text '63.64² = 4050'.
17. Place a vertical red (#FF0000) arrow to the left of the fitted line and write the black (#000000) label '63.64 mm' beside it.
18. Below the left panel (approx 5%–48% x, 85%–95% y), add two lines of bold red (#FF0000) serif text: line 1 'Overfit (try to minimize the residuals ONLY)', line 2 'Fails to detect the Pattern'.
19. Below the right panel (approx 52%–95% x, 85%–95% y), add two lines of bold red (#FF0000) serif text: line 1 'Generalized (Residuals are not minimized)', line 2 'Successes to detect the Pattern'.

20. Apply a serif typeface (Times New Roman-like) to all text: captions bold and slightly larger than the black equation/annotation text, equation text regular weight, badge numeral bold; keep 'ONLY' and 'Pattern' capitalized exactly as written.
